html:
The Pee Dee are a Native people of north-eastern South Carolina, along the Great Pee Dee River, which is named after them. Their language is unknown; they are often grouped with the Siouan-speaking peoples of the Carolina Piedmont, such as the Catawba.

They farmed maize and hunted deer in the river valley, and from the late 1600s they traded deerskins and, at times, captives with English traders from Charles Town in the Province of Carolina. Epidemics and the Yamasee War of 1715 broke many small peoples of the region. Some Pee Dee joined the Catawba; others stayed in the river swamps, mixed with settlers, and were later recognised by the state of South Carolina. Their neighbours on the coast were the Waccamaw.
